messages.author: 3444f9129095f179
messages.subject: hyper prior doesn't converge
parts:
How would you interpret this? I have a model where the many hi have hyper prior h.

h ~ nornal(1, 1)
hi ~ normal(h, 1)

hi do converge but h does not. Did I give too little variance to h? Since h is not important can I ignore the non convergence?

Dirk

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] hyper prior doesn't converge
parts:
You're model's not well identified well here. You usually
want to allow a scale parameter for hi. And you might be
better off with a non-centered parameterization.

If you unfold it into standard normal components (the
non-centered parameterization) its easy to see where
the identifiability issues arise:

h_raw ~ normal(0, 1);
hi_raw ~ normal(0, 1);
hi = 1 + h_raw + hi_raw;

There is only one h_raw and presumably many hi_raw, so they're
not symmetric.

- Bob
